title: What's new from Anthropic and what's next: Alex Albert
talk_summary: A product/marketing keynote announcing Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Artifacts, Projects, and tool-use APIs, framed around the 'electricity didn't improve factories until layouts were redesigned' analogy. The only concretely transferable engineering ideas are model-generation planning assumptions, PR-based eval methodology, and grounding outputs in shared project knowledge.

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure complex multi-step reasoning by having the model iteratively write and test its way through real pull requests, scoring pass rates rather than using academic benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one of the best methods that we found for actually measuring more complicated chains of reasoning is pull request
takeaways.numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 64% vs Claude 3 Opus 38% on internal PR evals

takeaways.technique: Plan for models getting cheaper/faster on months-not-years cadence
takeaways.what_they_do: They advise building roadmaps assuming a smarter, cheaper, faster model arrives during development, so architecture shouldn't hard-code one model's cost/limits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: models will become smarter cheaper and faster in orders of months not years
takeaways.numbers: 3.5 Sonnet cited at $3/M input, $15/M output, 5x cheaper than 3 Opus

takeaways.technique: Projects: ground outputs in shared curated knowledge
takeaways.what_they_do: They let teams attach style guides, codebases, transcripts, and past work to a shared project so model outputs are grounded in that context and chats/artifacts are shared instead of docs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: projects enables Dev teams to work and collaborate much more efficiently by grounding cla's outputs in your own knowledge

takeaways.technique: Tool-use API with many client-side tools and structured JSON output
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose custom client-side functions to the model and note devs give it hundreds of tools at once, plus consistent structured JSON output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I've actually started to seen devs give Claude hundreds of tools at a time

takeaways.what_they_do: They added a tool that writes an optimized prompt from a task description, plus editable templates with variables for testing RAG cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we added a prompt generator that uses Claud to write prompts for you based on a task description
